scope: Read-only adversarial review of the current S103 v7 Gate0 and formal execution chain. No GPU/model execution and no future payload access.

findings.finding: The formal bundle preparer executes the caller-supplied --validator and accepts its JSON, but never requires that validator SHA to equal protocol.validator_ref.sha256. It also accepts caller-supplied --sealer and --sbatch and merely records their hashes after the fact; v7 contains no reviewed refs for the preparer, sealer, sbatch script, or launch guard. The launch guard repeats the same trust pattern: GWM_GATE0_V2_VALIDATOR can select the validator, and the guard only checks it against the dispatch manifest that the same permissive preparer created, not against protocol.validator_ref. test_s103_formal_chain.py lines 72-99 positively demonstrates this gap by creating a synthetic validator for a protocol with no validator_ref and expecting bundle creation to succeed.
findings.impact: A caller-controlled validator can emit zero-error PRE_RUN_READY, while a caller-controlled sbatch or sealer can alter mounts, run order, or seal semantics. Both the bundle and launch guard can therefore pass without executing the exact formal chain reviewed by Gate0, making a formal GPU result non-interpretable and bypassing Gate0.
evidence: GATE0_CONTRACT_CANDIDATE_v7.json: protocol binds predictor/scorer/verifier/validator but not preparer/sealer/sbatch/launch guard

findings.finding: Both assembler and validator treat reviewer identity as an unauthenticated, case-sensitive free-form string. different_reviewer only strips whitespace and compares raw strings. The protocol author codex-root-20260916 can therefore be accepted as a supposedly different reviewer under an alias or case variant such as CODEX-ROOT-20260916. The protocol reviewer is also not required to differ from the adapter reviewer.
findings.impact: The stated requirement for genuinely different review can be self-satisfied without another identity, so Gate0 independence is not enforced.

findings.finding: The scorer accepts any caller-supplied seal whose self-reported run_id, protocol SHA, predictor exit code and unauthorized-read count look valid. It does not require seal schema/status/future_scoring_permitted, does not bind a reviewed sealer SHA or launch-guard receipt, and does not require or verify the dispatch manifest SHA. The post-run validator likewise checks seal fields and timestamps but not trusted formal-dispatch provenance.
findings.impact: A prediction produced after future exposure can be paired with a freshly fabricated seal and scored as if it came from the isolated formal run. Timestamp ordering alone is self-asserted and does not establish causal pre-seal generation.

findings.finding: FORMAL_CHAIN_SOFTWARE_RECEIPT_20260916.json is stale relative to v7. It records formal_sbatch SHA 9dc445d3f90c63489a1b878bbe0ffd80df039a65d8f690d2887d91f54ce00fbe, while the current script SHA is b460b696118f3bfe3b40a1f893672de0acfbf8d3e6a0d21789a360f980a2011a, and its real-candidate negative control is still v5 rather than v7. The current readiness file asserts formal-chain PASS but does not repair this mismatched receipt.
findings.impact: The published PASS receipt cannot substantiate the current launch artifact set or the current v7 negative control, creating stale-evidence ambiguity at the GPU authorization boundary.

limitations: This was a static, read-only review of source, manifests, hashes, and metadata; no GPU/model execution or formal dispatch was performed.
No future RGB, depth, or pose payload was opened; scorer_inputs.json was treated as identity metadata only.
The review did not independently re-establish the original dataset calibration from sensor documentation or raw capture logs.
The exact-boundary receipt was inspected as evidence but its prior H800 execution was not repeated.
recommended_action: Keep S103 v7 blocked and do not submit the formal GPU job or accept post-run scores.

Create a new reviewed protocol revision that binds exact SHA descriptors for the bundle preparer, sealer, Slurm script, launch guard, generic launcher, and validator in addition to predictor/scorer/verifier.

Make prepare_formal_bundle_s103.py reject every supplied validator, predictor, sealer, and sbatch artifact whose path/bytes/SHA do not exactly match the reviewed contract; make the launch guard independently repeat those contract-to-bundle checks and require all bundle members to share the intended immutable bundle root.

Require scorer and post-run validator to verify a trusted dispatch manifest, bound sealer identity, launch-guard receipt, seal schema/status/future flags, and exact prediction-output descriptors before any future payload is opened.

Replace free-form reviewer strings with authenticated reviewer attestations or an allowlisted canonical identity scheme using case-folded comparison; require adapter and protocol reviewer identities to be distinct if two-person review is intended.

Add negative tests for a fake PRE_RUN_READY validator, modified sbatch, modified sealer, reviewer alias/case spoofing, and a fabricated prediction seal; then regenerate a v7-or-later formal-chain receipt whose recorded hashes match every current artifact.
